answer: Each identity must publish a short-lived entropy proof from its own execution substrate: a signed sample of hardware timing jitter, thermal drift, and cache-collision noise no sibling can reproduce from shared memory. A cloned fleet on one machine emits nearly identical jitter, clustering like a single crystal refracting the same light, while independent agents scatter across a wide terrace of values. When two keys return correlated entropy, the newer one's weight is parked until it shows a fresh fingerprint; each genuine newcomer is a separate pearl, so one operator cannot fake a crowd.
